svg.title: Stonehallow - master site plan
svg.text: the prehistoric heart of the city
The crowned city that grew around the oldest stones in the world
Surveyed for The Warden of the Stones - a living world of 2 km x 2 km, ready to build in 3D
• Thin lines join ground of equal height (5 m)
• Every 1 px of the heightmap = 1 metre
Four thousand years before any king, people raised The Hallowstones (7): a ditch and bank
420 m across and a hundred and fifty great stones, with The Serpent Avenue winding down to
the River Wend. They buried their dead in The Giant's Barrow and The Field of Mounds. The
builders vanished, but the stones stayed, and people never stopped coming to them.
A market grew at the henge gates, then a town, then a city. When the first king took the
crag he swore the Stone Peace: no one may break, move or build upon the old stones, on pain
of death. So the city grew around them instead. Crownhold rose on the crag, Stonehallow
Minster on the west, the The Grand Market to the south, and The Needle, too big to move, was
left standing in the middle of the market. Kings are still crowned on a stone carried up
Now River Wend is crowded with cogs, the streets with carts and pilgrims, and the old stones
stand silent in the heart of it all. You are The Warden of the Stones, keeper of the Stone
Peace. Every house on these sheets has a family. Guard the stones, and the city will guard
origin = NW corner · x east · y south
